summary: Cefiderocol is a parenteral siderophore cephalosporin reserved for carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative infections, including CRE, carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) and difficult-to-treat Pseudomonas aeruginosa. It enters bacteria via iron-transport systems (Trojan horse) and inhibits cell-wall synthesis. The usual adult dose is 2 g IV every 8 hours as a 3-hour infusion, adjusted for renal function.
indications: Complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI), including pyelonephritis, caused by susceptible Gram-negative organisms
Hospital-acquired bacterial pneumonia and ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonia (HAP/VAP) caused by susceptible Gram-negative organisms
Infections caused by carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacteria (CRE, CRAB, difficult-to-treat P. aeruginosa) with limited treatment options

moa: Cefiderocol is a bactericidal siderophore cephalosporin that chelates ferric iron and enters Gram-negative bacteria through iron-transport channels (Trojan-horse uptake), concentrating in the periplasmic space. It then binds penicillin-binding protein 3 (PBP-3) and inhibits peptidoglycan cell-wall synthesis, causing cell lysis. The siderophore entry plus stability against many beta-lactamases (including KPC, OXA-48-like, NDM and other metallo-enzymes) gives activity against carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, Acinetobacter baumannii and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to cefiderocol or other cephalosporins
relative: History of immediate-type penicillin or carbapenem allergy (cross-reactivity risk)
Severe renal impairment without dose adjustment
monitor: Patients with seizure risk or CNS disorders

preg: There are no adequate well-controlled studies in pregnancy. Animal studies showed no direct fetal harm at clinically relevant exposures. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed and the benefit outweighs the risk.
lact: It is unknown whether cefiderocol is excreted in human milk. Consider the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding alongside the mother's clinical need and any potential risk to the infant.
renal: Cefiderocol is eliminated primarily by the kidneys, so the dose must be adjusted by creatinine clearance. Standard 2 g q8h (3-hour infusion) applies at CrCl 60-119 mL/min; give 2 g q6h if CrCl >= 120 mL/min (augmented clearance), 1.5 g q8h at CrCl 30-59, 1 g q8h at CrCl 15-29, and 0.75 g q12h at CrCl < 15 mL/min (with or without hemodialysis). On hemodialysis days give the dose after dialysis. For CRRT, dose by effluent flow rate per the label table.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is expected in hepatic impairment; cefiderocol is eliminated renally as largely unchanged drug.

major: No major contraindicated drug interactions established
moderate: Nephrotoxic drugs (aminoglycosides, potent diuretics) - additive renal risk; monitor renal function
Iron preparations - theoretical interaction with iron-dependent uptake; clinical significance unclear
minor: Live typhoid/BCG vaccines - antibacterials may reduce efficacy
Oral anticoagulants - cephalosporins may rarely prolong prothrombin time
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive urine glucose with copper-reduction methods and a positive direct Coombs test.

serious: Seizure/neurotoxicity (class risk, especially with renal impairment)
Increased all-cause mortality signal vs best available therapy in CREDIBLE-CR (carbapenem-resistant infections)

Signs of hypersensitivity, particularly in beta-lactam-allergic patients
Complete blood count, electrolytes and liver enzymes on prolonged therapy
Neurologic status in renal impairment; evaluate persistent diarrhea for C. difficile
Clinical response and susceptibilities; de-escalate when a narrower agent applies
counsel: Given as a 3-hour IV infusion in a healthcare setting on a strict every-8-hour schedule
Report rash, hives, swelling or difficulty breathing immediately
Tell staff about any penicillin, cephalosporin or carbapenem allergy
Report severe or persistent diarrhea during or after treatment
Complete the full course of therapy
pk: Dosing every 6-12 hours by renal function maintains levels
Store vials per label; use reconstituted and diluted solutions within labeled beyond-use time
pearls: Reserve agent: restrict to documented or highly suspected carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative infection with stewardship oversight
The 3-hour infusion and renal-adjusted interval are part of efficacy; augmented clearance (CrCl >= 120) needs q6h dosing
Covers KPC, OXA-48-like and metallo-beta-lactamases (NDM, VIM, IMP) that defeat most beta-lactams
Note the CREDIBLE-CR mortality signal in carbapenem-resistant infections; weigh benefit vs risk and monitor closely
missed: For scheduled inpatient dosing, give the missed dose as soon as possible and adjust the schedule so the interval to the next dose matches the renal-adjusted interval; do not give two doses together. Maintain the 3-hour infusion for each dose.
overdose: No specific antidote. Overdose, particularly in renal impairment, may cause neurologic sequelae including encephalopathy and seizures. Manage supportively; cefiderocol is removed by hemodialysis, which can lower serum levels.
